clues.title: Plate: long white, one blue strip
text: Romania uses standard long, **white** European plates with a single **blue strip** on the left.
clues.summary: Standard long white European plates with a single blue strip on the left.

clues.title: Language: Latin letters Ă Â Î Ș Ț
text: Romanian is a Romance language similar to Italian, containing the following special letters:
- Ă ă
- Ș ș
- Ț ț
These letters are also found in some other European languages:
- Â â, used in French, Portuguese and Turkish
- Î î, used in French, Turkish and Italian
Additionally, in Turkish you can find the letter Ş, which can be confused with the Romanian Ș.

images.caption: Romanian text with Ă Â Î Ș Ț shown large

clues.summary: A Romance language close to Italian, with the special letters Ă, Ș and Ț. Â and Î also appear in French and Turkish, and Turkish Ş looks like Ș.

clues.title: Pole: concrete with holes to the bottom
text: The most common types of utility poles in Romania are **holey poles** with the holes going all the way to the bottom. The holes are typically either quite wide or quite tall.

NOTE: Poland and Hungary also both use holey poles. [Polish](https://goo.gl/maps/chLemRYUZcz7DDFL6) holey poles do not have holes near the bottom and [Hungarian](https://www.google.com/maps/@47.6425626,20.0330594,3a,75y,313.1h,93.94t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sKeSZXDk8-kk4EYn1mVYf3Q!2e0!7i16384!8i8192) holey poles generally have smaller holes than in Romania.

images.caption: Perforated concrete poles compared: Hungary (left), Poland (centre), Romania (right)

clues.summary: Concrete poles with holes running all the way down, either wide or tall. Poland's have no holes near the bottom, and Hungary's holes are smaller.

differs.how: holes do not reach the bottom of the pole

clues.title: Pole: round concrete
text: **Round concrete poles** are also quite common.
NOTE: These are very similar to poles found in Bulgaria.
clues.summary: Round concrete poles are also common. Bulgaria has very similar ones.

clues.title: Pole: white painted bottoms on trees and poles
text: Trees and poles will often have **white painted bottoms**.
NOTE: This is also common in Ukraine and parts of Russia.
clues.summary: Trees and poles often have white painted bottoms. Also common in Ukraine and parts of Russia.

clues.title: Pole: extra large yellow sticker with town name
text: This type of extremely **large yellow pole** sticker is specific to Romania.

Beware that [smaller stickers](https://goo.gl/maps/2Dme6waEUjKguFWWA) are also common and that both [Bulgaria](https://goo.gl/maps/TnBDLBKuq3V8JjLc9) and [Hungary](https://goo.gl/maps/dvBUfMAjvm63LBC17) can have similar ones.
NOTE: The town or city name will typically be written close to the middle of these stickers. In this case Podu Iloaiei is written.
clues.summary: A very large yellow pole sticker with the town name near the middle. Smaller stickers are common too, and Bulgaria and Hungary can have similar ones.

clues.title: Pole: two support bars, upside-down triangle
text: Two support bars holding up the metal bar on pole tops, resembling an upside down triangle, can sometimes be found in Romania.
NOTE: Czechia, Slovakia, Albania and Serbia also feature this pole top.
clues.summary: Two support bars hold up the metal bar on top of the pole, forming an upside-down triangle. Czechia, Slovakia, Albania and Serbia use it too.

clues.title: Route marker: waystone with road number
text: It is very common to see **waystones** in Romania. They are typically fairly large, with red or blue framing with the road number on the side, or made of actual stone and somewhat rugged-looking. There is also a very small variant which is all white.
clues.summary: Waystones are very common: large ones with red or blue framing and the road number on the side, rugged real stone ones, or a tiny all-white version.

clues.title: Road lines: short dashes, narrow gaps
text: While there are many types of roadlines in Romania, these outer lines, consisting of **short dashes** with **narrow spaces**, can be a good clue for the country.
clues.summary: Edge lines made of short dashes with narrow gaps are a good clue, though many line types exist.

clues.title: Road lines: thick centre line
text: Middle lines are often noticeably **thicker** than average. This is especially useful to tell Romania apart from Bulgaria, which generally has [thinner road lines](https://goo.gl/maps/6nK1dEjs41bLrkPt5).

images.caption: Centre lines compared between two countries, labelled RO (left) and BG (right)

clues.summary: Centre lines are often noticeably thicker than average. This helps tell it from Bulgaria, which has thinner lines.

clues.title: Sign: blue arrow signs with road number
text: Romanian directional signs are blue, arrow shaped, and have a white border. They will very often display the **road number**, which can be either **red or **[**blue**](https://goo.gl/maps/62EzegUJUrbSQHwQ6).
clues.summary: Blue arrow-shaped direction signs with a white border. They very often show the road number in red or blue.

clues.title: Sign: yellow speed sign with skyline, white name below
text: The most common type of town entry sign in Romania is a **yellow sign** displaying a speed limit and a city skyline, with a **white sign** displaying the town name below.

NOTE: The upper sign can also either be [white](https://goo.gl/maps/nAGuvAEn4CDn1iQu5) or [completely absent](https://www.google.com/maps/@43.9295577,23.865666,3a,15y,60.5h,84.85t,358.78r/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sXfkr8gj25si9PKl8IgR9Ew!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: The usual town entry is a yellow sign with a speed limit and a city skyline, and a white name sign below. The top sign can also be white or missing.

clues.title: Sign: black backs
text: Romanian sign backs are often **black**.
NOTE: This is also common in Italy, Albania and Germany.
clues.summary: Road sign backs are often black. This is common in Italy, Albania and Germany too.

clues.title: Chevron: red on white, yellow frame
text: Romanian chevrons are **red on white**, often with a **yellow frame**.
NOTE: Several eastern and central European countries have the red on white chevrons, however yellow frames are by far the most common in Romania.
clues.summary: Red on white chevrons, often with a yellow frame. Many central and eastern European countries use red on white, but yellow frames are most common here.

clues.title: Bollard: thin white, red strip near top
text: Romanian bollards are thin and white, with a **red vertical strip** near the top. It is worth noting that bollards in Romania are somewhat rare.
NOTE: Turkey has a very similar bollard.
clues.summary: Thin white bollard with a red vertical strip near the top. Bollards are fairly rare here, and Turkey has a very similar one.

clues.title: Sign: yield sign with very thick red border
text: This yield sign, with an extremely **thick red border**, with a **thin white outline**, is unique to Romania. Beware that different yield signs also exist in Romania.
clues.summary: A yield sign with an extremely thick red border and a thin white outline is unique here. Other yield signs exist too.

clues.title: Houses: pastel stone, orange tile or grey metal roofs
text: Romanian architecture primarily consists of single-family houses made of stone, typically painted in different pastel colours and with roofs ranging from orange tiles to grey metal. It is also somewhat common to see houses with walls made of [painted square tiles](https://goo.gl/maps/up6x7Wpuc8ovmBk7A) in different patterns.
clues.summary: Mostly single-family stone houses in pastel colours, with roofs from orange tiles to grey metal. Walls covered in painted square tiles are also fairly common.

clues.title: Landscape: mountains in centre, flat farmland around
text: The Romanian landscape ranges from tall forested mountains and hills in the centre to flat or rolling agricultural landscapes in the south, west and east.
clues.summary: Tall forested mountains and hills in the centre, with flat or rolling farmland in the south, west and east.

clues.title: Haystack: stick straight through the middle
text: This type of **haystack**, typically featuring a stick going straight through, is very common in Romania.

images.caption: Haystacks built around a stick standing straight through the middle

clues.summary: Haystacks with a stick going straight through the top are very common.

clues.title: Cars: Dacia is the most common brand
text: Dacia is the most common car brand in Romania, making up more than a quarter of all vehicles in the country.
NOTE: No other eastern European country has more than 10% Dacias.

images.caption: Dacia cars, the most common brand, parked side by side

clues.summary: Dacia makes up over a quarter of all cars. No other eastern European country has more than 10% Dacias.

clues.title: Landscape: high centre and north, flat south and west
text: This is an **elevation map** of Romania. The tallest mountains are found in the middle and north of the country, while the south and west are particularly flat.
clues.summary: The tallest mountains are in the middle and north, while the south and west are very flat.

clues.title: Landscape: completely flat fields, hills on horizon
text: **Completely flat** agricultural landscapes can be found in the south and west.
NOTE: If you can see distant hills or mountains to the north, you are likely in the south, and if you see them to the south or east, you are likely in the west.
clues.summary: Totally flat farmland in the south and west. Hills far to the north mean south; hills to the south or east mean west.

clues.title: Houses: almost all orange tiled roofs
text: If you see several houses and almost all of them have **orange tiled roofs**, you are likely to be in the western half of the country.
clues.summary: If nearly every house has an orange tiled roof, you are likely in the western half.

clues.title: Houses: metal or plastic fake-tile roofs
text: Similarly, if you see several houses and almost all of them have **metal** or **plastic fake tiled roofs**, you will probably be in the eastern half of the country.
clues.summary: If most houses have metal or plastic roofs shaped like tiles, you are probably in the eastern half.

clues.title: Villages: long straight street, short side to road
text: Villages near the Hungarian border will often be built in the **same style** as villages in Hungary. This style can be summarised as having long, straight streets with single-storey houses being evenly spaced along the road, typically having the short side of the house facing the road. The vast majority of roofs will have orange tiles.
clues.summary: Near the Hungarian border, villages look like Hungarian ones: long straight streets, single-storey houses evenly spaced with the short side facing the road, and mostly orange tiled roofs.

differs.how: use other clues, villages look the same

clues.title: Landscape: rolling farm valleys at a NNW-SSE angle
text: South of Iași, near the border to Moldova, you can find rolling agricultural valleys with a very specific **north-north-west** to **south-south-east** angle.
NOTE: Make sure to look for agricultural fields on top of the hills to confirm this region.
clues.summary: In the far east near the border, rolling farm valleys run north-north-west to south-south-east. Look for fields on top of the hills.

clues.title: Sign: two languages, with Hungarian
text: Bilingual signs with **Hungarian** are mostly found in the central regions of Covasna, Harghita and Mureş, but also less commonly near the Hungarian border.
clues.summary: Signs in two languages including Hungarian are mostly in the central counties of Covasna, Harghita and Mureș, and less often near the Hungarian border.

clues.title: Gates: elaborately decorated wooden
text: Elaborately **decorated wooden gates** are commonly found in the region of Maramureș.

images.caption: Elaborately decorated wooden gate with a shingled roof

clues.summary: Elaborately carved wooden gates are common in the north, in the Maramureș region.

clues.title: Plants: sunflowers
text: **Sunflowers** are primarily found in the far east of the country, and secondly in the far west.
clues.summary: Sunflower fields are mostly in the far east, and second most in the far west.

clues.title: Street signs: unique design per city
text: Several Romanian cities and towns have **unique street signs**. This infographic covers all with a population above 100 000.

images.caption: Romanian street name signs compared: Bucharest sector, Galati and Constanta designs on a map

clues.summary: Many bigger cities and towns have their own street sign design. The infographic covers all with more than 100,000 people.

clues.title: Road lines: all yellow on a mountain road
text: The 67C is a mountain road with **all** **yellow road lines**.
clues.summary: The 67C mountain road has all its lines painted yellow.

clues.title: Landscape: dramatic mountain road
text: The 7C is recognisable as going through some of the most **dramatic mountains** in Romania. The highest point on the road is right by the border between Sibiu and Argeș.
clues.summary: The 7C passes through some of the most dramatic mountains in the country. Its highest point is near the Sibiu and Argeș border.

clues.title: Windows: squinting-eye shape
text: This type of window, shaped like a **squinting eye**, is most commonly found in the city of Sibiu.

images.caption: Roof windows shaped like a squinting eye, circled in red at the top left

clues.summary: Windows shaped like a squinting eye are most common in the city of Sibiu.

clues.title: Coverage: mountains in Gen 2 camera
text: If you see a **mountainous landscape** in **Generation 2**, you are likely close to Brașov.
clues.summary: Mountain scenery seen with the older Gen 2 camera usually means near Brașov.

clues.title: Coverage: flat land in Gen 2 camera
text: **Flat landscapes** in **Generation 2** are mostly found near Bucharest.
clues.summary: Flat land seen with the older Gen 2 camera is mostly near Bucharest.

clues.title: Coverage: green boat trekker in canals
text: A **boat trekker**, with a green boat, can be found in the far east of the country. It mostly goes through small, overgrown canals in a flat landscape.
NOTE: There is no road coverage in this region.
clues.summary: A boat camera with a green boat in the far east, going through small overgrown canals in flat land. There is no road coverage there.

clues.title: Language: useful words
text: Here are a few words in Romanian that can either help you identify the language quickly, be helpful in region guessing, or just help learn the general feel of the language:
**piese (auto)** - car parts
**cu excepţia** - except (with exception)
**preţ** - price
**de vânzare** - for sale
**magazinul** - SHOP
**preturi mici** - low prices
**Bucuresti** - Bucharest
**amenda** - fine
**interzisă** - prohibited
**plajă** - beach
**stradă** - street
**bulevard** - avenue
**atenţie** - attention
**biserică** - church

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Handy words: piese (auto) car parts, preț price, de vânzare for sale, magazinul shop, amenda fine, plajă beach, stradă street, biserică church.

clues.title: Language: stradă (street) and relatives
text: Stradă is the word for street in romanian. It's often shortened to "str." Careful! It can often be seen without the breve which makes it the same word as the italian "strada", however, most streets in Italy use the word "via".
Here are some other words similar to street in romanian: **bulevard/bulevardul** - avenue/boulevard **piaţă** - square/market **calea** - way **intrarea** - entry/entrance **aleea** - alley

images.caption: Blue street sign reading Str. Lipscani

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Stradă means street, often shortened to str. Without the breve it looks like Italian strada, but Italy mostly uses 'via'. Also: bulevard, piață square, calea, intrarea, aleea.

differs.how: Italian streets mostly say 'via', not strada

clues.title: Language: spotting it from letters and endings
text: Romanian is a romance language and thus more similar to **Italian**/French/Spanish then to the languages of it's neighboring countries. It also uses many unique characters and patterns that make it easy to recognize with a little bit of practice.
**ă ș ț, unique characters**
Â â, used in French, Portuguese and Turkish
Î î, used in French, Turkish and Italian
Common words: și, de, la, a, ai, ale, alor, cu
Word endings: -a, -ă, -u, -ul, -ului, -ție (or -țiune), -ment, -tate;
names ending in -escu
Double and triple i: copii, copiii
Note that Romanian is sometimes written online with no diacritics, making it harder to identify. A cedilla is sometimes used on S (ş) and on T (ţ) instead of the correct diacritic, the comma (above).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Closer to Italian, French and Spanish than to its neighbours. Look for ă ș ț, common words like și and de, endings like -ul, -ție, -tate and names ending in -escu.

clues.title: Route marker: red, blue and white km marker
text: Within Europe, those red/blue/white **KM markers** are unique to **Romania**, the color representing the color the road will show up on the map.
**How to use:**
On the side is the road number and usually on the front are two cities, the first one is the closest **largest** city and the second one is the closest town.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Red, blue or white km markers are unique in Europe, and the colour matches the road's colour on the map. The side shows the road number; the front shows the nearest big city, then the nearest town.
